PAA molecular weight, dispersity, molar amount basis, supplier and reagent purities are not specified. FeCl3 hydration state is not specified; no hydrate is substituted.
The stock is described by 50 mmol NaOH in 20 mL DEG, without a measured final volume or stated molarity. The reaction receives only the stated aliquot, not the full stock charge.

Reaction vessel geometry, pressure, nitrogen flow, heating ramp and injection rate are not quantified. The temperature drops from 220 °C to about 210 °C after injection; the subsequent one-hour temperature is not separately specified.

Wash volumes, separation method, speed/time, exact repetition count and final dispersion concentration are not reported. Methods say several washes; the dispersibility discussion mentions three ethanol/water washes.

source_notes.label: Separate the cluster size from primary crystal size
source_notes.summary: The authors assemble primary magnetite crystals into larger flowerlike clusters. TEM measures the overall cluster diameter, whereas HRTEM or Scherrer estimates describe the primary crystals. These sizes remain distinct: a 93 nm cluster has a reported 9.65 nm Scherrer grain size.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 1–3, Cluster model, Figures 1–3

source_notes.label: Why use poly(acrylic acid)
source_notes.summary: The authors attribute the PAA choice to coordination of carboxylate groups with iron cations on magnetite. Uncoordinated carboxylate groups extending into water are proposed to provide dispersibility. Surface coverage, chain configuration and a unique polymer molecular graph are not measured.

source_notes.label: Proposed hydrolysis and growth mechanism
source_notes.summary: The paper proposes that hot DEG/FeCl3/PAA with NaOH produces water and increases alkalinity, favoring hydrolysis. DEG is proposed to partly reduce Fe(OH)3 to Fe(OH)2, followed by dehydration to Fe3O4. Primary crystals then nucleate and aggregate into clusters; HRTEM alignment is interpreted as oriented attachment with subsequent high-temperature sintering. These are source interpretations, not directly isolated intermediate recipes.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 1–2, Hydrolysis/growth discussion, Figure 2; cited references 3, 6, 19 and 20

source_notes.label: Stock aliquot controls the reported cluster series
source_notes.summary: Keeping the other stated method conditions fixed, the paper varies NaOH/DEG aliquot volume from 1.60 to 1.85 mL and reports six cluster diameters from 31 to 174 nm. The suggested explanation is a change in water concentration and alkalinity that affects FeCl3 hydrolysis. Neither pH nor water concentration is quantitatively measured in the main.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 1, 4, Size-control discussion and Experimental Section

source_notes.label: Magnetic response without a large single crystal
source_notes.summary: The cluster series remains superparamagnetic at room temperature despite its larger overall size. The authors compare strong cluster magnetic response with an 8 nm reference nanodot, and propose that interactions among the primary crystals differ from those of a single crystal. The 93 nm sample has remanence and coercivity at 2 K. No measured critical size for every cluster or temperature-dependent phase change is inferred.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 1, 3, Magnetic discussion and Figure 4

source_notes.label: Mass normalization and fitted moment have different meanings
source_notes.summary: Saturation magnetization is reported per gram of PAA-covered particles. The paper suggests higher polymer mass fraction or surface disorder as possible reasons for lower small-particle values. Moment per cluster is separately obtained from a Langevin fit and is an author-derived result. The SI fit details and XAS data are not reviewed in this main-only contribution.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 3, Figure 4c and adjacent discussion

source_notes.label: Application outlook is distinct from demonstrated performance
source_notes.summary: The authors propose uses in separation, targeted delivery and MRI, as well as future silica coating for ligand coupling. The main demonstrates field-induced chaining, magnetic separation and redispersion; it does not provide a biomedical validation, silica-shell synthesis or ligand-coupling recipe.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 3–4, Figure 5 and outlook; reference 21

source_notes.label: Reference nanodots and sample-unresolved field response
source_notes.summary: The 8 nm nanodots have no supplied main-text preparation. Figure 5 demonstrates study-level CNC field response without exact cluster-size identity. Both contexts are retained without additional recipe/pair credit.
